#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Issue batch B7 (#146) — the one tree copy every proof that BUILDS the app
in a copy gets its copy from.

    python3 tools/proof/tree_copy.py --selftest

A proof that builds a mutant app must not build in the tree: xcodegen writes
`FrameJob.xcodeproj/`, `app/Info.plist` and `app/FrameJob.entitlements`, and
the helper's build step runs `bun install` and `bun build`, which write into
`agent/`. So the copy's `app/` and `agent/` are COPIED (`COPIED`), and every
other build input is a SYMLINK to the tree's — `core` already built, so
`project.yml`'s pre-build `cargo build --release` is a no-op and the copy
links the tree's `libframejob_core.a`.

**The build inputs are derived from `project.yml`, not listed by hand.**
`build_inputs` answers every top-level directory of the tree (no leading
`.`, not in `GENERATED`) whose name `project.yml` spells as `NAME/` not
preceded by a name character — `app/Sources`, `$PROJECT_DIR/core`,
`"$PROJECT_DIR/agent/build.sh"`. So a build step that reads a new top-level
directory is linked into every copy the day it lands, and no builder's copy
can miss it (#146: `graphics_proof.py`'s copy missed `agent/` and `docs/`).
`GENERATED` (`build`, `FrameJob.xcodeproj`) is never linked: a copy writes
its own. The one exception is `build/codecs` (road map "codec-export" C0, spec
§11 CX-5): the copy's `build/` is a real directory and its `build/codecs` a
symlink to the tree's, whether or not that exists yet, so a copy never builds
the encoders itself — `tools/codecs/build_codecs.py` resolves its own path to
the tree's and reuses (or, on a key change, rebuilds under its lock) the tree's.

`make_copy(dest, agent=True)`, in order: remove `dest` (`remove_tree`), make it; copy `app/`
without `Info.plist` or `*.entitlements`; copy `project.yml`, `Makefile`
and `VERSION` (`COPIED_FILES`: the copy's own `make project` reads all
three, spec §11 PUB-2); when `agent`, copy `agent/` without `node_modules`; link every
other build input; make `build/` and link `build/codecs` to the tree's. It answers `(dest, None)`, or `(None, reason)` on an
`OSError`. `agent=False` is the assistant spike's, which splices
Rasterize's `agent/` in its place.

**A copy builds through `build_app(dest, seconds, env=None,
release_only=None)`** (issue batch B88): `make app-debug` or `make app` in
`dest`, as `proof_app.config(release_only)` chooses (`RC_PROOF_APP`), under
`bounded.run`'s wall-clock bound, answering `(the copy's Frame Job.app, None)`
or `(None, reason)`: the target, its status, whether it expired, and its
first six `error:` lines (else its output's tail). A build that succeeded
prints one line with its target and its seconds.

**A built app is unregistered before its folder goes** (#223). Xcode and
`/usr/bin/open` register a `.app` with LaunchServices, and deleting the
folder leaves the registration behind. `unregister_apps(path)` runs
`lsregister -u` on every `*.app` holding `Contents/Info.plist` at or under
`path` (never descending into a found `.app`, `Intermediates.noindex`,
`node_modules` or `.git`, never following a symlink, never raising), and
`remove_tree(path)` is it followed by `shutil.rmtree`. Every proof that
deletes a folder that can hold a built `.app` deletes it through
`remove_tree`.

The selftest, in a fresh `work/tree_copy/`:

* T1 — the tree's `project.yml` names `agent`, `app`, `core`, `docs`,
  `graphic` and `tools`, and neither `GENERATED` name;
* T2 — a copy's `app/` is a real directory holding `Sources/main.swift` and
  no `Info.plist` or `*.entitlements` at its top; its `agent/` is real, holds

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Issue #378 — `ExportWriter`'s readers, one per output (spec §11 #378, amending G-17):
the MP4/MOV writer reads the video composition output and the audio mix output on an
`AVAssetReader` each, and each pump cancels only its own reader, on its own queue, after its
own last read — CX-15 (2) and (6) applied to `ExportWriter`, as C3 proved them for WebM.

    python3 tools/proof/export_readers_proof.py [--app debug|release|PATH]
    python3 tools/proof/export_readers_proof.py --readers       # R2, R3 alone, no app
    python3 tools/proof/export_readers_proof.py --faults        # F1–F4 alone, on the app
    python3 tools/proof/export_readers_proof.py --mutant NAME

Launches its own instances of the chosen app (`proof_app.py`: `--app`, else
`RC_PROOF_APP`, else Debug; a build older than its inputs is refused) on scratch sockets,
works under `tools/proof/work/export-readers/`, closes every project it opens with
`discard: true` and stops each instance by its own PID. It reuses `av1_export_proof.py`'s
instance, documents, exports and readers, and `webm_export_proof.py`'s projects, chapter
and sound readers, its fault row (`fault_row`) and its readers probe (`readers_rows`).
ffprobe and ffmpeg only READ the files.

Rows (`<ID> ok|FAIL — <detail>`, then `scores: n/m`; exit 0 iff all passed):

* Z1 — every instance's log is silent (no `Frame Job: `, `Svt[` or `SVT-AV1: ` line).
* C1 — A1's project with its two chapters (`webm_export_proof.a1_doc`) exported `h264` on
  an instance launched with `-RCDevExportFault audio@1000000` (a fault that never fires):
  done, 150 decoded frames, 240,000 audio samples, ffprobe's chapters "Intro" 0–2.5 s and
  "Body" 2.5–5 s, and the writer's readers line exactly `video 2, audio 2` (both readers
  read to their end, 2 = completed: a clean export cancels no reader).
* C2 — a project holding only a 5 s text clip, exported `h264` on the same instance: done,
  exactly one stream, and the readers line exactly `video 2, audio none` (a silent movie
  has no audio reader).
* R2, R3 — the measurement behind the change, `webm_readers_probe.swift` (no app; the
  tree's export shaders as its `default.metallib`): A1's project read through
  `ExportWriter`'s two outputs on one reader and on two, each on a thread of its own, from
  builds of their own, at `h264`'s settings — R2 the 16-bit decode, R3 the float mix a
  normalised export reads (8 bytes a frame): 150 frames each, every frame's 64RGBAHalf
  bytes equal, and 240,000 frames of sound equal sample for sample.
* F1–F4 — G-17's windows closed on `ExportWriter`: W9's 24-clip 1080p project
  (`webm_export_proof.long_doc`) exported on an instance launched with
  `-RCDevExportFault` (`ExportWebMDevFault.writerKey`): F1 `audio@40` on `h264` (the audio
  pump fails at its 40th read), F2 `video@30` on `h264` (the video pump fails at its 30th
  append), F3 `audio-hold@40` on `h264` (the audio pump held 3 s at its 40th read, before
  the read, and `cancel_export` sent when the hold's log line appears), F4 the same hold on
  `av1` (whose video pump is `ExportEncodePump`, its reader cancelled by the writer's block
  queued behind the pump's read loop). Each ends — F1 and F2 `failed` naming the dev fault,
  F3 and F4 `cancelled` — within 10 s of the fault's log line (F3, F4: of the cancel), with
  no file at the path, and the writer's `framejob export dev readers:` line reads exactly
  `video 4, audio 4`: both readers cancelled (status 4) by their own pumps, and two readers
  (the line adds ` (one reader)` when the outputs share one).

Mutants (`--mutant NAME`, a tree copy built as Debug with the named anchor replaced, the F
rows alone run; exit 1 and `MUTANT CAUGHT` when exactly the named rows fail):

  shared-reader          the audio output put on the video's reader: F1–F4
  no-own-cancel          the plain pump's own `cancelReading` on a stop dropped: F1–F4
  encode-cancel-dropped  the block that cancels the `av1` row's video reader dropped: F4

An instrument that cannot run is a FAIL, never an exit.
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import av1_export_proof as av1  # noqa: E402
import mcp  # noqa: E402
import proof_app  # noqa: E402
import webm_export_proof as webm  # noqa: E402

WORK = HERE / "work" / "export-readers"
av1.WORK = WORK            # the reused Instance and mutant builder work here
FRAMES = 150
SAMPLES = 240_000          # 5 s at 48 kHz
FAULT_KEY = "RCDevExportFault"
FAULTS = {"F1": ("audio@40", "failed", "h264"), "F2": ("video@30", "failed", "h264"),
          "F3": ("audio-hold@40", "cancelled", "h264"),
          "F4": ("audio-hold@40", "cancelled", "av1")}
F_ROWS = list(FAULTS)
READER_ROWS = ("R2", "R3")

SOURCES = "app/Sources"
WRITER = f"{SOURCES}/ExporterWriter.swift"
MUTANTS = {
    "shared-reader": {"rows": F_ROWS, "anchors": [
        (WRITER,
         "            audioReader = hasAudio ? try AVAssetReader(asset: built.composition) : nil\n",
         "            audioReader = hasAudio ? videoReader : nil\n")]},
    "no-own-cancel": {"rows": F_ROWS, "anchors": [
        (WRITER, "            if self?.isStopping ?? true { reader.cancelReading() }\n",
         "            if self?.isStopping ?? true && false { reader.cancelReading() }\n")]},
    "encode-cancel-dropped": {"rows": ["F4"], "anchors": [
        (WRITER,
         "                if let self, self.isStopping { self.videoReader?.cancelReading() }\n",
         "                if let self, self.isStopping && false { self.videoReader?.cancelReading() }\n")]},
}

results = {}


def check(ident, ok, detail):
    results[ident] = bool(ok)
    print(f"{ident} {'ok' if ok else 'FAIL'} — {detail}", flush=True)


def readers_lines(instance):
    """The writer's readers lines so far, each after `readers: `."""


# ---- the mutants -------------------------------------------------------------------

def run_mutant(name):
    if name not in MUTANTS:
        print(f"unknown mutant {name}; the mutants are {sorted(MUTANTS)}")
        return 2
    named = sorted(MUTANTS[name]["rows"])
    print(f"mutant {name}: building the copy", flush=True)
    av1.MUTANTS = MUTANTS
    app, copy = av1.build_mutant(name)
    if app is None:
        print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — {copy}")
        return 2
    logs = []
    try:
        run_fault_rows(app, logs)
    except Exception as error:  # an instrument that cannot run is the control's failure
        print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — {error}")
        return 2
    failing = sorted(k for k, v in results.items() if not v)
    print(f"mutant {name}: named {named}, failing {failing}")
    if named == failing:
        print(f"MUTANT CAUGHT: {name}")
        return 1
    if not set(named) & set(failing):
        print(f"MUTANT SURVIVED: {name}")
        return 0
    print(f"MUTANT CAUGHT, NOT EXACTLY: {name}")
    return 3


# ---- main --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def scores():
    print(f"scores: {sum(results.values())}/{len(results)}")
    return 0 if all(results.values()) else 1


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="ExportWriter's readers, one per output (#378)")
    parser.add_argument("--app", help="debug, release or a .app path (default RC_PROOF_APP)")
    parser.add_argument("--mutant", help="one of " + ", ".join(MUTANTS))
    parser.add_argument("--readers", action="store_true",
                        help="R2 and R3 alone: two readers against one, no app")
    parser.add_argument("--faults", action="store_true", help="F1–F4 alone, on the app")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.app:
        os.environ[proof_app.ENV] = args.app
    WORK.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if args.mutant:
        return run_mutant(args.mutant)
    if args.readers:
        run_reader_rows()
        return scores()
    try:
        app = proof_app.bundle()
        proof_app.require_fresh(proof_app.executable(app))
    except (proof_app.StaleApp, ValueError, OSError) as error:
        check("Z0", False, f"the app cannot be driven: {error}")
        return scores()
    print(f"app {app}", flush=True)
    logs = []
    if args.faults:
        run_fault_rows(app, logs)

## C4 — VP9 in WebM, 8-bit and Profile 2 HDR

### Record

**Built 2026-10-28** in `~/devel/framejob-codecs` (branch `codecs`, on C3's `e759112`), not yet
committed or merged.

**Decision first.** CX-16 in `designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md` before any code:
- (1) the `vp9_webm` row after `av1_webm`: `writer` `libvpx`, no `encoder_speeds`, an HDR row, even-sized, `optimize_for_network` inert;
- (2) one speed (CX-3 binds), so the sheet's Speed popup is disabled on it — the brief's "Speed popup mapped to cpu-used" is not built;
- (3) the depth by picture: `sdr` Profile 0 8-bit I420 BT.709, `hlg`/`pq` Profile 2 10-bit I010 BT.2020, with `g_profile` set as `validate_config` demands;
- (4) the WebM `Colour` as the only transfer label;
- (5) no CodecPrivate;
- (6) keys and packets;
- (7) capped CQ;
- (8) the calibration, filled in after the run;
- (9) the C wrappers;
- (10) the SDR rewrap labels, added by RULING-1 below.

"Amended by CX-16" lines sit under CX-8, CX-15, HD-5, HD-14 (c), HD-18 (b) and HD-19 (b), and the index has the matching rows.

**What landed.**
- **Core** (no format bump, no new `rc_*`):
  - `export_encoder.rs`: `Writer::Libvpx` and `Writer::takes_speed`.
  - `export_table.rs` (582 lines): the row (`PRESETS: [Preset; 14]`). `takes_encoder_speed` is `writer.is_some_and(takes_speed)`, and `to_json` gives `encoder_speeds` only where speeds apply.
  - `export.rs`: `writer` on every writer row, `encoder_speed` on the AV1 rows alone.
  - `dynamic_range.rs`: six `HDR_ROWS`, and the 8-bit sentence names `vp9_webm`.
  - `webm_layout.rs` (222): `codec_private_hex` optional, plus the four new refusals.
  - `webm_ebml.rs` (401): `video_entry(codec_id, Option<private>, …)`.
  - `container_codec.rs`'s `vpcc` answers the keyframe's matrix; `container.rs` publishes it as `describe`'s `stream_matrix` (RULING-1).
  - The header: the presets, settings, webm and container paragraphs.
- **Core tests:** `export_vp9.rs` (6) and `webm_writer_vp9.rs` (5, including the stream matrix per colour space); VP9 headers and layouts in `common/webm.rs`. Updated: `webm_writer_refusals.rs`, `export.rs`, `export_av1.rs`, `export_size.rs`, `dynamic_range.rs` and `canvas_output.rs`.
- **Swift:**
  - `app/Bridging/FrameJobVPX.h`, the two wrappers.
  - `ExportVideoEncoder.swift`: the protocol, `ExportEncodedPacket` and `ExportRateTable`, which SVT's `crf` now goes through with the same values (P1).
  - `ExportVP9Encoder.swift` (238 lines).
  - `ExportEncodePump`: the encoder chosen by `writer`, `webmCodec`, an optional `formatDescription`.
  - `ExportI010`: `bitDepth` and the `framejob_export_i420` kernel.
  - `ExportAV1Picture.cicp` and `ExportWebMLayout.VideoCodec`.
  - The WebM writer's guard; the MP4 sink's optional format.
  - `ExportPreset.writer` and `Applies.softCap`; `codecFactor` takes `vp9`.
  - The catalog's preset, size, `video_bitrate`, `dynamic_range` and `encoder_speed` descriptions.
  - `ContainerRewrap.Video.streamMatrix` and `ContainerRewrapWriter.sdrLabels` (RULING-1).
- **Documents:**
  - Spec §7.1, §7.4, §7.7, §7.8, §7.9a and §7.10, and the spec index.
  - The guide's export, HDR, MCP and projects-and-media pages, and the README.
  - `docs/manual-checks.md`: SE-19, and HDR-2's and HDR-8's VP9 lines.
  - `tools/proof/README.md`'s C4 section.
- **Proofs:**
  - `vp9_export_proof.py` (Z1, V1–V11, S1, P1, R1–R3, ten mutants) and `vp9_rate_probe.swift`.
  - `export_offset_proof.py` E41, E42.
  - `hdr_proof.py` H7s and its mutant `sdr-copy-unlabelled`.
  - The sentence constants in `av1_export_proof.py` (H5), `hdr_proof.py` (DR) and `hevc_alpha_proof.py` (`B6_SIZE`).
  - `av1_export_proof.py`'s `av1-not-hdr` re-anchored onto the six-row `HDR_ROWS`.

**RULING-1 (the orchestrator, 2026-10-28): V10's STOP, option (a).**
- **The finding.** V10 re-imported Frame Job's own 640 × 360 SDR `vp9_webm` and read R/G/B 11.83 / 0.78 / 5.65 of 255 from the source project's render: cyan (0, 255, 255) came back (23, 255, 255).
- **The cause.** That is BT.709 decoded as BT.601. The copy's description carried no colour (HD-18 (b): "no other copy's description changes"), so AVFoundation chose the matrix by the picture's size. The same round trip at 1280 × 720 read 0.53 / 0.16 / 0.30.
- **The ruling.** Fix the import in this phase, decision first. That is CX-16 (10): an SDR copy carries the colour its source states.
  - From its Colour: matrix and primaries 1, 5, 6 or 9, and transfer 1, 6, 13, 14 or 15, as Core Video names them.
  - Else, for the matrix, a VP9 keyframe's `color_space`: CS_BT_709 → 1, CS_BT_601 and CS_SMPTE_170 → 6, CS_BT_2020 → 9.
  - With neither, nothing.
  - The PQ and HLG rules are unchanged.
- **After the fix.** V10 reads 1.90 / 0.55 / 0.96 (Debug). `hdr_proof.py` H7s on Debug, with two 640 × 360 `smptebars` VP9 WebMs:
  - the BT.709-tagged copy is labelled, and renders 1.06 / 0.86 / 1.35 from ffmpeg's BT.709 decode (4.41 / 12.80 / 3.44 from the BT.601 one);
  - the untagged copy is unlabelled and renders 0.96 / 0.81 / 1.39 from BT.601, as before.
  - Its mutant `sdr-copy-unlabelled` exits 0 (`MUTANT PASS`, H7s alone failed: the tagged render 3.86 / 13.08 / 2.79 from BT.709). `vp9_export_proof.py`'s mutant of the same name catches V10 alone.
- **Re-runs on Debug** (the ruling asked for them):
  - `container_import_proof.py` 16/16 and `codec_import_proof.py` 10/10. Their VP9 fixtures (ffmpeg's `testsrc2` through libvpx-vp9) state no colour (ffprobe: unknown ×3), so their copies are unchanged.
  - `hdr_proof.py` H7, H7d, H7p, H7o, H7r, H7w, H7h, H7s and Z1 ok.
  - **H7i FAIL on an instrument precondition, not on this change.** Its byte half compares with a control capture (`work/t3-1/ctl/h7-pq_plain.png`) that exists on neither this worktree nor main. Its oracle half held: both files 1 level from the oracle. Its fixtures are MOVs, which the rewrap does not touch.
- **A finding, not pinned.** H7w's two SDR WebMs (`sdr_webm_cll`, `sdr_webm_plain`, BT.709 ×3, 1024 × 128, 10-bit) are now labelled, where they were not. H7w compares them only with each other, and still passes.
- **A note on the copy's colour fields.** The copy's ffprobe fields read BT.709 even without the label, from the `vpcC` record and the bitstream, so H7s's field check alone cannot see the label. Its render check does.

**The calibration** (CX-16 (8) has every figure):
- **Method.** VMAF pairs frames by index. The first owner run paired by timestamp and read 76.17 at CQ 30 / Low; re-scored by index, about 91.
- **(a) Spike half.** Cells 34 / 30 / 26 / 24 / 16; the largest cap share was 1.143 ×.
- **(b) Owner, 8-bit.** Cells 34 / 26 / 20 / 18 / 14. The owner's clip binds every cell, and every kept file is 0.79–0.95 × the cap.
- **(c) Owner, 10-bit** (HLG at `hlg`, against `hevc_10bit`). Cells 34 / 28 / 26 / 24 / 20, every kept file 0.75–0.86 × the cap. Format default was lowered to 24 after Release R3 (below).
- **No cell missed its comparator**, so there was no product STOP.
- **The table** is 8-bit 34 / 26 / 20 / 18 / 14 and 10-bit 34 / 28 / 24 / 24 / 20.
- **The guide** says about 1.15 × the cap.

**Commands run and what they printed.**
- **Targeted, core:**
  - `cargo test --release` over `export_vp9`, `webm_writer_vp9`, `webm_writer`, `webm_writer_refusals`, `export`, `export_av1`, `export_size`, `dynamic_range` and `canvas_output` passed: canvas_output 7, dynamic_range 7, export 38, export_av1 11, export_size 20, export_vp9 6, webm_writer 8, webm_writer_refusals 4, webm_writer_vp9 4.
  - After RULING-1, `webm_writer_vp9` 5, `container` 11, `container_timing` 15 and `webm_writer` 8 passed.
  - `cargo fmt --check` and `make lint` were clean.
- **Targeted, Swift:** `make typecheck` exited 0 with the four baseline warnings after each Swift step. `make app-debug` succeeded each time.
- **`vp9_export_proof.py` on Debug:**
  - The first run scored 12/14: V10 failed (the STOP) and P1 failed (placeholder table).
  - After RULING-1 it scored 13/14 (V10 1.90 / 0.55 / 0.96; P1 still the placeholder).
  - `--probe` read 1/1 after the table was filled and again after R3's change.
- **Mutants (Debug copies):**
  - Each of the ten exited 1 with `MUTANT CAUGHT` on exactly its rows:
    - `vp9-not-hdr`: V8, V9 and cargo `dynamic_range`.
    - `hdr-at-8-bits`: V8.
    - `sdr-at-10-bits`: V1 and V8.
    - `transfer-unlabelled`: V8.
    - `no-hdr10-in-webm`: V8.
    - `kf-interval-default`: V3.
    - `full-range-8bit`: V4.
    - `speed-on-vp9`: V7, S1 and cargo `export_vp9`.
    - `sdr-copy-unlabelled`: V10.
    - `all-key`: V3 and V10. Its first run was `CAUGHT, NOT EXACTLY`, because V10 failed too (R/G/B ≈ 125, the copy's every sample a sync sample). V10 was added to its rows and the re-run exited 1.
  - `av1_export_proof.py --mutant av1-not-hdr`, re-anchored, exited 1 with `MUTANT CAUGHT` on H1, H2, H4, S3 and cargo `dynamic_range`.
  - `hdr_proof.py --only H7s,Z1 --mutant sdr-copy-unlabelled` printed `MUTANT PASS`.
- **Offset rows on Debug:** `export_offset_proof.py --only E38,E39,E41,E42` scored 4/4. E41 and E42 read median −0.043 ms, every flash on its frame.
- **`make gate`:**
  - First run: names 1 s, typecheck 12 s, fmt 3 s, lint 15 s, test 290 s, app 190 s, `gate: PASS 511s`.
  - After R3's change: test 123 s, app 108 s, fmt and lint skipped, `gate: PASS 238s`.
- **Release:**
  - `vp9_export_proof.py --rate`, first run: 16/17. R3 failed: `hevc_10bit` 95.692 against `vp9_webm` at CQ 26 95.679. The cell went to 24.
  - Second run: **17/17**.
    - R1 (Format default): `hevc` 95.469, `vp9_webm` 95.498 at 0.938 × the cap.
    - R2 (High): 95.777 against 95.882 at 0.948 ×.
    - R3 (HLG): `hevc_10bit` 95.692 against 95.958 at 0.893 ×.
    - V10: 1.89 / 0.54 / 0.93.
  - `webm_export_proof.py` 29/29; `av1_export_proof.py` 19/19.
  - `export_offset_proof.py --only E36,…,E42` on a Release instance: 7/7, its log free of `Frame Job: `.
  - `hdr_proof.py --only DR,Z1` 2/2; `hevc_alpha_proof.py` 43/43.

**Findings.**
- **libvmaf pairs frames by timestamp**, and a WebM's whole-millisecond block times put a third of a 30 fps clip against neighbours. Every VMAF of a WebM here pairs by index. AV1's R rows are MP4 and unaffected.
- **VideoToolbox's comparator moves run to run.** `hevc` at Format default read 95.338 in one Release run and 95.469 in the next; `hevc_10bit` in the HLG project read 95.620 in the calibration and 95.692 at R3. C2 saw the same. A cell kept by a few hundredths can fail its R row. 8-bit Format default (+0.029) and Medium (+0.016) are thin, and R1 passed against both readings.
- **A copy marks sync samples by the container's key flag.** A WebM whose every block is flagged key previews garbage at a seek (`all-key`'s V10), which is why the key flag must be libvpx's.
- **SD SDR WebM imports** (RULING-1, above).

**CLAUDE.md edits owed** (the integrator's):
- **Root `CLAUDE.md`:**
  - The file map's `ExportI010.metal` line becomes "the bundled encoders' 64RGBAHalf → planar 10-bit I010 (or, for `vp9_webm`'s SDR picture, 8-bit I420) conversion".
  - Architecture's WebM sentence reads "the WebM file an `av1_webm` or `vp9_webm` export writes".
- **`core/CLAUDE.md`:**
  - `export_encoder.rs`: `Writer::Libvpx` and `takes_speed`.
  - The `webm_*` entry: `V_VP9` with no CodecPrivate and BitsPerChannel 8 or 10.
  - `dynamic_range.rs`: "the six HDR rows", `vp9_webm` among them.
  - `container_codec.rs`/`container.rs`: `vpcc`'s stream matrix and `describe`'s `stream_matrix`.
- **`app/CLAUDE.md`:**
  - New entries for `ExportVideoEncoder.swift` (the protocol, `ExportEncodedPacket`, `ExportRateTable`), `ExportVP9Encoder.swift` and `app/Bridging/FrameJobVPX.h`.
  - `ExportI010` converts to 8-bit I420 too.
  - `ExportEncodePump` picks SVT-AV1 or libvpx by `writer`.
  - `ContainerRewrapWriter`'s entry gains the SDR labels (CX-16 (10)).

**Owed.**
- **Manual checks:** SE-19 (`vp9_webm` in Chrome, Firefox and Safari, 8-bit and HLG; re-import on another Apple silicon Mac) and HDR-8's VP9 half.
- **H7i's control capture**, which no tree on this host holds.
- **Still to come:** C5 (VP9 alpha) and C6.

**The calibration** (CX-16 (8) has every figure):
- **Method.** VMAF pairs frames by index. The first owner run paired by timestamp and read 76.17 at CQ 30 / Low; re-scored by index, about 91.
- **(a) Spike half.** Cells 34 / 30 / 26 / 24 / 16; the largest cap share was 1.143 ×.
- **(b) Owner, 8-bit.** Cells 34 / 26 / 20 / 18 / 14. The owner's clip binds every cell, and every kept file is 0.79–0.95 × the cap.
- **(c) Owner, 10-bit** (HLG at `hlg`, against `hevc_10bit`). Cells 34 / 28 / 26 / 24 / 20, every kept file 0.75–0.86 × the cap. Format default was lowered to 24 after Release R3 (below).
- **No cell missed its comparator**, so there was no product STOP.
- **The table** is 8-bit 34 / 26 / 20 / 18 / 14 and 10-bit 34 / 28 / 24 / 24 / 20.
- **The guide** says about 1.15 × the cap.

**Commands run and what they printed.**
- **Targeted, core:**
  - `cargo test --release` over `export_vp9`, `webm_writer_vp9`, `webm_writer`, `webm_writer_refusals`, `export`, `export_av1`, `export_size`, `dynamic_range` and `canvas_output` passed: canvas_output 7, dynamic_range 7, export 38, export_av1 11, export_size 20, export_vp9 6, webm_writer 8, webm_writer_refusals 4, webm_writer_vp9 4.
  - After RULING-1, `webm_writer_vp9` 5, `container` 11, `container_timing` 15 and `webm_writer` 8 passed.
  - `cargo fmt --check` and `make lint` were clean.
- **Targeted, Swift:** `make typecheck` exited 0 with the four baseline warnings after each Swift step. `make app-debug` succeeded each time.
- **`vp9_export_proof.py` on Debug:**
  - The first run scored 12/14: V10 failed (the STOP) and P1 failed (placeholder table).
  - After RULING-1 it scored 13/14 (V10 1.90 / 0.55 / 0.96; P1 still the placeholder).
  - `--probe` read 1/1 after the table was filled and again after R3's change.
- **Mutants (Debug copies):**
  - Each of the ten exited 1 with `MUTANT CAUGHT` on exactly its rows:
    - `vp9-not-hdr`: V8, V9 and cargo `dynamic_range`.
    - `hdr-at-8-bits`: V8.
    - `sdr-at-10-bits`: V1 and V8.
    - `transfer-unlabelled`: V8.
    - `no-hdr10-in-webm`: V8.
    - `kf-interval-default`: V3.
    - `full-range-8bit`: V4.

    - `sdr-copy-unlabelled`: V10.

    - R1 (Format default): `hevc` 95.469, `vp9_webm` 95.498 at 0.938 × the cap.
    - R2 (High): 95.777 against 95.882 at 0.948 ×.
    - R3 (HLG): `hevc_10bit` 95.692 against 95.958 at 0.893 ×.

C2 saw the same. A cell kept by a few hundredths can fail its R row. 8-bit Format default (+0.029) and Medium (+0.016) are thin, and R1 passed against both readings.

**`vp9_export_proof.py`** imports `webm_export_proof.py`'s and `av1_export_proof.py`'s helpers
and works under `work/vp9-export/`; its docstring has every row. In short: V1 the streams
(`vp9` Profile 0 `yuv420p`, Opus) and the walk's `V_VP9` TrackEntry with no CodecPrivate and
Colour 1/1/1/Range 1/8 bits; V2 a clean decode, 150 frames, 240,000 samples; V3 the key rule,
each block's key flag against its first frame's VP9 header (show_existing 0, frame_type 0);
V4 the SDR picture against `hevc` at 20 Mb/s as yuv420p (frames 0–149 and the stripes
fixture's patches); V5 chapters and the range; V6 a cancel with no file; V7 `encoder_speed`
refused; V8 HLG, PQ and SDR — Profile 2/2/0, the tags, `trace_headers`' `color_space`, the
walk's Colour and PQ's HDR10; V9 the HDR pictures against `hevc_10bit` as yuv420p10le; V10
Frame Job's re-import of V1's and V8's files, and V1's media rendered at 3 s against the
source project's render (≤ 8/255 per channel); V11 the silent movie; S1 the sheet (Format "VP9
(WebM)", the Speed popup drawn disabled, footnote "VP9 · WEBM"); P1 `vp9_rate_probe.swift`
(no app): `SVTAV1Encoder.crf` and `VP9Encoder.cqLevel` against the tables, through the shared
`ExportRateTable`; R1–R3 (`--rate`) the owner's clip, each `vp9_webm` file ≤ 1.30 × the cap
with VMAF ≥ `hevc`'s (SDR, Format default and High) or `hevc_10bit`'s (HLG, Format default).
**VMAF pairs frames by index** (`settb=1/30,setpts=N` on both inputs): a WebM's block times are
whole milliseconds, and libvmaf's timestamp pairing put a third of the owner clip's frames
against a neighbour's (measured in C4's calibration).

The mutants (`--mutant`, a tree copy built as Debug, every row but P1 and R): `vp9-not-hdr`
V8, V9 and cargo `dynamic_range`; `hdr-at-8-bits` V8; `sdr-at-10-bits` V1, V8;
`transfer-unlabelled` (the HLG and PQ transfers 2 in the layout) V8; `no-hdr10-in-webm` V8;
`all-key` V3, V10 (the copy's every sample a sync sample, so the 3 s render decodes an inter
frame as a key); `kf-interval-default` V3; `full-range-8bit` V4; `speed-on-vp9` V7, S1 and
cargo `export_vp9`; `sdr-copy-unlabelled` (the rewrap's SDR labels dropped, CX-16 (10)) V10.

**`hdr_proof.py` H7s** (CX-16 (10), the ruling on C4's STOP): two 640 × 360 `smptebars` VP9
WebMs by ffmpeg, one BT.709-tagged and one untagged; the tagged copy renders within 3/255 of
ffmpeg's BT.709 decode, the untagged one's copy stays unlabelled and renders as AVFoundation's
BT.601 reading at that size. Its mutant `sdr-copy-unlabelled` fails H7s alone.

# 06 — fix notes, pass 1 (RULING-2)

Worktree `~/devel/framejob-codecs` (branch `codecs`), on top of `e2af96e`. The changes are uncommitted, for the orchestrator to amend into the commit.

## Findings

1. **Nit 1 — fixed.** `ExportRateTable.value` (app/Sources/ExportVideoEncoder.swift) now calls `preconditionFailure("ExportRateTable.value: an empty rate table")` on an empty table, so it can no longer answer 0. The doc comment says why.
2. **Nit 2 — fixed.** `VP9Encoder.send`'s bit-depth guard (app/Sources/ExportVP9Encoder.swift) now sets `broken = true` before it throws. The refusal is the encoder's own sentence: "The VP9 encoder was opened for N-bit pictures and was sent a M-bit one." No proof matched the old text.
3. **Nit 3 — fixed.** `ContainerRewrapWriter` now has `sdrPrimaries: Set<Int> = [1, 5, 6, 9]` beside `sdrMatrices`, and the primaries check uses it.
4. **Nit 4 — fixed.** H7s in `tools/proof/hdr_proof.py` now compares the untagged SD WebM's copy with a copy made by a tree before CX-16 (10).
   - **The comparison.** It is byte for byte, except for the `mvhd`, `tkhd` and `mdhd` wall-clock times that `AVAssetWriter` stamps. It reuses `video_configuration_proof.same_movie`. The control file is `<control>/h7s-sdr_untagged_webm.mov`.
   - **Capture.** `capture DIR --only H7s,Z1 --app <app>` writes that file. In capture mode the row scores only that the file was written.
   - **Documents.** The module doc and `tools/proof/README.md`'s C4 section describe the comparison.
   - **Where the control came from.** I ran `git archive d0f9fe0` into an isolated scratch folder and cloned `build/codecs` into it; `tools/codecs`, the Makefile and project.yml are identical at the two commits. Its own `make app` (Release) succeeded. I captured into `tools/proof/work/c4/h7s-ctl` and fixed its `capture.json` provenance by hand (the proof writes the worktree and "debug"). I then copied the file into the H7i control below.
   - **Control on the old build.** I ran H7s with `d0f9fe0`'s app against its own capture. The untagged half held: both copies are 3,544 bytes, 3 boxes masked, sha `adca300496aad871`. The labelled half failed, 3.86/13.08/2.79 from the BT.709 decode, as it must.
   - **Cleanup.** The scratch build was removed through `tree_copy.remove_tree`, which unregisters it from LaunchServices.
5. **RULING-2 item 2, H7i's control — done.**
   - I ran `cp -cR ~/devel/framejob/tools/proof/work/i378/hdr-ctl` into the worktree's `tools/proof/work/i378/hdr-ctl`.
   - It holds `h7-pq_plain.png`, so H7i ran against it and passed.
   - Its `capture.json` names tree `framejob-lane-b` and config `debug`. Those come from the last capture (the SI addition).
6. **RULING-2 item 3, re-verification — done.** The results are below.
   - **Skipped:** `export_gain_proof --against tools/proof/work/i378/gain-before`. Main's checkout has no `gain-before`; its `work/i378/` holds only `hdr-ctl`.
7. **RULING-2 item 4 — done.** `designs/codec-export.md` has a new "### Fix pass 1 (2026-10-28): the rebase onto main and the review's nits" section under C4. It covers the rebase, the nits, H7i's control, every result and the mutants. The "H7i's control capture" bullet is gone from Owed.

## Verification

### Targeted
- `make typecheck`: exit 0, with exactly the four baseline warnings (CompositionBuilder ×2, +Orientation, Exporter).
- **Mutant anchors.** Every anchor of every mutant in `av1_export_proof`, `vp9_export_proof` (10), `hdr_proof` (91), `hevc_alpha_proof`, `webm_export_proof`, `export_readers_proof` and `export_offset_proof` occurs exactly once in the merged tree.
  - That includes `export_readers_proof`'s three anchors in the merged `ExporterWriter.swift`: `shared-reader`, `no-own-cancel` and `encode-cancel-dropped`, each count 1.
